guide_line: Find rms speed and average kinetic energy from temperature.
steps: In the kinetic-molecular model, gas particles are tiny next to the container, move in straight lines, and bounce with no energy loss.
Average kinetic energy per mole depends only on kelvin temperature: KE = (3/2) RT. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K). Two different gases at the same temperature have the same average KE per mole.
The root-mean-square speed is u = sqrt(3RT/M). Put M in kg/mol by dividing g/mol by 1000. The speed is then in m/s. Lighter particles move faster. A higher temperature also raises the speed.

worked_example.q: What is the rms speed of He at 300.0 K, in m/s? He is 4.0026 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K).

similar_problem.q: What is the rms speed of Ne at 300.0 K, in m/s? Ne is 20.180 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
similar_problem.hint: Change 20.180 g/mol into 0.020180 kg/mol, then take sqrt(3 × 8.314 × 300.0 / M).

problems.q: What is the rms speed of He at 298.15 K, in m/s? He is 4.0026 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K) and M in kg/mol.
What is the rms speed of N2 at 298.15 K, in m/s? N2 is 28.014 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
hints: N2 is 0.028014 kg/mol. Square-root 3RT/M at 298.15 K.

problems.q: What is the rms speed of O2 at 500.0 K, in m/s? O2 is 31.998 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
hints: O2 is 0.031998 kg/mol, and this temperature is 500.0 K rather than room temperature.

problems.q: What is the average kinetic energy, in J, of 1.000 mol of ideal gas at 300.0 K? Use KE = (3/2) RT and R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
hints: Multiply 1.5 by 8.314 and by 300.0 K for one mole.

problems.q: What is the average kinetic energy, in J, of 1.000 mol of ideal gas at 600.0 K? Use KE = (3/2) RT and R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
problems.why: KE = (3/2)(8.314)(600.0) = 7483 J. Twice the kelvin temperature doubles the energy.
hints: This sample is at 600.0 K. Multiply 1.5 by 8.314 and by 600.0.

problems.q: At 300 K, which gas has the higher rms speed, He or Ar? He is 4.0026 g/mol and Ar is 39.948 g/mol. Type the formula.
problems.why: u = sqrt(3RT/M). Same T means the smaller mass, He, has the higher speed.
hints: Both gases are at 300 K, so the lighter one is faster. Type He.

problems.q: At the same temperature, what is u(He)/u(Ar)? He is 4.0026 g/mol and Ar is 39.948 g/mol. Report the number only.
hints: Temperature cancels. The speed ratio is sqrt(39.948/4.0026).

problems.q: N2 has an rms speed of 515.0 m/s. N2 is 28.014 g/mol. What is the temperature in kelvin? Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K) and T = u^2 M / (3R), with M in kg/mol.
For one gas, what is the ratio of rms speeds at 400.0 K and 300.0 K? Report u(400.0 K)/u(300.0 K).
hints: The mass cancels, so this speed ratio is sqrt(400.0/300.0).

problems.q: Do He and N2 have the same average kinetic energy per mole when both are at 300 K? Type yes or no.
problems.why: KE = (3/2) RT. The identity of the gas is not in that equation, so yes.
hints: Average kinetic energy per mole depends only on kelvin temperature, so type yes.

problems.q: As temperature rises, does the rms speed of a gas increase or decrease? Type increase or decrease.
problems.why: Speed grows with the square root of kelvin temperature, so it increases.
hints: u = sqrt(3RT/M), so a higher kelvin temperature raises the speed. Type increase.

problems.q: What is the rms speed of Ar at 273.15 K, in m/s? Ar is 39.948 g/mol. Use R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
hints: Ar is 0.039948 kg/mol. Use T = 273.15 K inside sqrt(3RT/M).

problems.q: Gas-law temperatures use which scale? Type its symbol.
problems.why: Add 273.15 to Celsius to get kelvin. The symbol is K.
hints: The gas laws use the kelvin scale. Type the capital symbol K.
